root_cause.text: The `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range` function performed unchecked array indexing into `rqstp->rq_pages[rc_curpage]` without verifying that `rc_curpage` remained within the bounds of the allocated page array (`rq_maxpages`), allowing out-of-bounds memory access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `if (head->rc_curpage >= rqstp->rq_maxpages) return -EINVAL;` before the first array access in the loop, and the CVE description explicitly states the function "indexed rqstp->rq_pages[rc_curpage] without verifying rc_curpage stays within the allocated page array." The vulnerability was introduced in commit d7cc73972661 which added support for multiple Read chunks per RPC, suggesting the page indexing logic was not properly validated when that feature was implemented.

The function iterates through pages using `info->ri_pageno` as an index into `rqstp->rq_pages` (line: `head->rc_arg.pages[info->ri_pageno] = rqstp->rq_pages[info->ri_pageno]`), but there is no bounds checking to ensure `info->ri_pageno` stays within `rq_maxpages`. The vulnerability allows unchecked array indexing into the page array, enabling out-of-bounds memory access.
